title: The Train Ride Out of Birmingham to the Factory at Bournville
conflicts: Workforce: 200 (Cadbury World fact sheet) and a first trainload of 230 vs 'fewer than 300 hands' (Gardiner 1923); story says about 200. Building start: January 1879 (Cadbury) vs March 1879 (Alexander 1906, Gardiner); story says early 1879. Arrival: September 1879 (fact sheet, Birmingham City Council) vs October (Gardiner); story gives both. Acreage 14.5 vs about 15; story uses 14.5. The brothers' quoted sentence differs by one word between the two books ('greatest' vs 'greater'); story quotes Alexander. Cadbury's site gives George the 'thousand pounds a year' remark, Gardiner gives it to Richard; not used.
notes: Core sources are two public-domain biographies on archive.org (Richard's daughter, 1906; Gardiner's Life of George Cadbury, 1923) plus Cadbury, Cadbury World, Birmingham City Council and a National Archives catalogue description. Funding set to bootstrapped (family-owned, self-financed; no external capital is recorded for the move). Arc kept as hard-responsibility; change-of-direction would also be defensible. Quote stance: complicates (self-interest and benevolence).
